subject.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits

question: Should ClawSweeper adopt this Linux namespace and Landlock contract as the mandatory repair-execution boundary and land containment, validation identity, and authenticated publication together?
rationale: Only maintainers can accept the self-hosted runner compatibility change and decide whether the combined credential-bearing boundary is complete enough to deploy.

options.title: Prove and land together
options.body: Require current-head hosted proof and a final audit of all pre-containment inputs and Git continuations, then accept the Linux/Landlock contract as one rollout.

options.title: Split the rollout
options.body: Land immutable Git publication separately and defer mandatory target containment until its runner compatibility and sandbox completeness are independently proven.

options.title: Preserve broader runners
options.body: Add an explicit compatibility mode while keeping strict containment opt-in, accepting a larger permanent policy surface.

recommendation.title: Prove and land together
recommendation.body: Require current-head hosted proof and a final audit of all pre-containment inputs and Git continuations, then accept the Linux/Landlock contract as one rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the clearest available context across the branch's validation, containment, and publication design and can route the final security decision to the appropriate repository owner.
